pass_a_gloss: [...] we name your name. It is a custom for the holy prophets to make supplications on behalf of Israel, for they were lovers of God and very well crowned with the glories toward piety. And since they once appeared from the root of Abraham and from blood of the holy fathers, they are necessarily gloomy as over kin, seeing those from Israel perishing through the impiety toward Christ. For this reason now too the blessed prophet Isaiah comes forward, saying: Lord our God, give peace to us; for you rendered all things to us. For if you should grant, he says, the peace to us, we will be full of every good, and we have received the most perfect sharing of the gifts from you. And what sort of peace they ask, it is necessary to see; for either they ask Christ himself, for he is our peace according to the Scriptures, and through him we were joined to the Father, through kinship, clearly the spiritual one. Or at least they say that: those not yet having believed, and having the stain from the sin not cast off, stand apart from God, and are rightly considered in the rank of enemies, and have a haughty neck, and fight the laws of the Master. But the obedient and easily reined, and ready toward anything whatever of the things pleasing to them, are both most dear and have peace toward him. But the thing is truly God-given, and coming through the generosity from above. Give us then, O Master, to be at peace toward you, and, the profane and loathsome sin having come out of the middle, to be united to you spiritually through a mediator, Christ. Such is the thing rightly said through the voice of Paul: Having been justified then from faith, we have peace toward God through our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ; which having happened we will be a possession and lot of God. For this reason wisely the 'Lord, possess us, outside you we know no other, we name your name' has been added. For those at peace toward him must be single-ways and yoked to God alone, so as both to know him only, and not even upon the tongue to carry the name of another wholly falsely named god. For it is needed to name him alone, because he alone is over us God by nature and in truth. Something such the law of the all-wise Moses also proclaimed to us: You will worship the Lord your God, and him alone you will serve, and by his name. Amen. [Lemma, Isaiah 26:14-15:] And the dead will not see life, nor will physicians raise up. Because of this you brought on, and destroyed, and took away every male of theirs. Add evils to them, Lord, add evils to all the glorious of the earth. Those who know only the one being God by nature and truly, and naming his name, and counting to him [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: It is the custom of the holy prophets to make supplications on behalf of Israel. For they were lovers of God and richly crowned with the glories of piety. And since they had sprung from the root of Abraham and from the blood of the holy fathers, they are of necessity downcast when they see those of Israel, as their own kin, perishing because of their impiety toward Christ. For this reason the blessed prophet Isaiah now comes forward and says: “Lord our God, give us peace; for you have rendered all things to us” (Isaiah 26:12). For if you grant us peace, he says, we shall be full of every good thing, and we shall have received in full the most perfect share in your gifts.

We must consider what kind of peace they ask for. Either they ask for Christ himself, for he is our peace, according to the Scriptures (Ephesians 2:14), and through him we have been joined to the Father, by kinship, that is, spiritual kinship. Or at least they mean this: those who have not yet believed, and whose stain of sin has not been cast off, stand apart from God and are rightly reckoned in the rank of enemies; they hold their necks high and fight against the laws of the Master. But those who are obedient and easily led, and ready for anything at all that those laws approve, are very dear to him and have peace with him. Yet this thing is truly given by God and comes through the generosity from above. Grant us, then, O Master, to be at peace with you, and, once profane and loathsome sin has been taken out of the way, to be united to you spiritually through Christ the Mediator.

Such is the word rightly spoken through the voice of Paul: “Therefore, since we have been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ” (Romans 5:1). When this has come about, we shall be God’s possession and his inheritance. That is why it is wisely added: “Lord, take possession of us; apart from you we know no other; we name your name” (Isaiah 26:13). For those who are at peace with him must be single-minded and yoked to God alone, so as to know him only and not even to carry on their tongue the name of any other, falsely named god at all. For we must name him alone, because he alone is God over us by nature and in truth. The law of the all-wise Moses proclaimed something of this kind to us: “You shall worship the Lord your God, and him only shall you serve, and by his name” (Deuteronomy 6:13; compare Matthew 4:10). Amen.

“But the dead will not see life, nor will physicians raise them up. Therefore you brought it upon them and destroyed them, and took away every male of theirs. Add evils to them, Lord; add evils to all the glorious of the earth” (Isaiah 26:14–15).
Those who know only him who is God by nature and in truth, and who name his name, and reckon to him …

choices.english: they had sprung from the root of Abraham
choices.why: The prophets are the subject: being of Abraham's root, they grieve for their kin.
rejected: Abraham's descendants have been destroyed from the root

choices.why: αὐτοῖς is taken of the nearest plural, the Master's laws.
φιλοτιμία here is God's open-handed giving, not ambition.
Those at peace with God must belong to him alone.
Isaiah 26:14 Septuagint reads ἰατροί; Cyril follows it.
